payload.comparison_population: obese asthmatic children with sufficient vitamin D
payload.symptoms: lower Forced Expiratory Volume in the first second, lower Functional Residual Capacity, lower Total Lung Capacity
payload.supporting_quote: Forced Expiratory Volume in the first second (84.5 ± 9.4 vs. 94.8 ± 8.4, P < 0.001), and Functional Residual Capacity (67.5 ± 20.1 vs. 79.3 ± 19, P = 0.01) were lower among vitamin D deficient obese asthmatics than their sufficient counterparts, and Total Lung Capacity was lower than their insufficient counterparts (86.9 ± 14.3 vs. 96.6 ± 10, P = 0.01)
Vitamin D deficiency was associated with pulmonary function deficits among obese children, but not among normal-weight children with asthma
